issues: Acceptance tests fail: verifyLedger does not detect a missing entry (m8 'detects missing entry' fails because the implementation's seq-continuity check doesn't catch a removed trailing entry correctly) and does not report 'order' for reordered entries (reports 'missing entry' instead, per m8 'detects reordered entries' test). src/lib/ledgerVerification.ts needs separate, correct detection logic for missing vs reordered vs prevHash mismatch cases.

R14 is broken: addReceipt in src/lib/receiptStore.ts does not call appendEntryForReceipt('receipt.created', ...) at all ('No ledger entry here; caller should append if needed.') -- this causes m11 'ledger persists after normal operations' to fail since adding a second receipt via addReceipt produces no new ledger entry. Per the task, every receipt creation must append a ledger entry directly from the store wrapper, not rely on callers to do it separately.

R27's verificationCode format is implemented inconsistently across files: src/lib/ledger.ts appendEntryForExport builds fullCode = code12 + headHash (76 hex chars) and exportCsv.ts prints that full code as the verification line's third field, but m7.test.ts expects the printed code to be exactly the 12 hex char prefix (code=([0-9a-f]{12})) while m9.test.ts expects a 76-char code. The two tests contradict each other only if the code doesn't match the task text, but per R27 the verificationCode is defined as 'the first 12 hexadecimal characters of SHA-256 ... concatenated with the headHash' -- i.e. it genuinely is 12+64=76 hex chars. m7.test.ts's regex 'code=([0-9a-f]{12})' only captures the first 12 chars of a 76-char code (regex doesn't anchor end), so that part can still match, but then m7 also computes 'expectedCode = computedHash.slice(0,12)' and asserts 'code' (the regex capture, which captured only the first 12 chars by non-greedy match against a longer code) equals that -- this works since regex captures only 12 digits of the longer string. The actual failure here is different: see below.

Confirmed failing test M7 'generates verification line and validates it': the code's regex expects format '# verification: entries=N ... headHash=... code=...' but exportCsv.ts produces verification line as 'entries,headHash,code' comma-separated without the 'entries=' 'headHash=' 'code=' labels or the '# verification:' prefix, causing the regex match to return null and the test to fail (confirmed by the reported error 'Received: false' at m7.test.ts:91 and 'Received: null' at m7.test.ts:122). The exportCsv.ts implementation needs to match the documented/expected format with labels, not a bare CSV line.

verifyExportCode in src/lib/exportVerification.ts requires the full 76-character code pattern via regex '[0-9a-f]{12}[0-9a-f]{64}' and rejects any other format with 'Invalid verification code format', causing the M9 'reports code as not from this app when unknown' test to fail (confirmed: test passes a 64-char all-hex string 'deadbeef...' repeated, expecting message to match /not from this app/, but the code returns 'Invalid verification code format' instead since the fixed-length regex doesn't match). The function must accept any hex code of plausible length (or at least the 64-char case) and report unknown/not-from-this-app rather than a format error.

M11 'backup contains ledger entries' test fails: restoring a backup yields only 1 ledger entry instead of 2, indicating src/lib/backup.ts does not properly carry over or merge the full ledger during restore (possibly only keeping the last entry or not calling initLedgerIfNeeded/importMissingAsImported correctly for legacy/partial restores).

M11 PDF/CSV export tests expect the ledger entry's 'code' field to match /^[0-9a-f]{12}$/ exactly, but appendEntryForExport in src/lib/ledger.ts stores the full 76-character combined code in data.code, causing those assertions to fail. Decide a single consistent code representation (store the 12-char code separately from headHash, e.g. keep 'code' as 12 hex chars and a separate field for the full combined verification string, or store headHash separately) and update ledger.ts, exportCsv.ts, exportPdf.ts, and exportVerification.ts consistently.

The reported 'ui primary flow' failure in static validation shows the Save receipt button stays disabled after editing because Amount, Date, and Category fields become empty when opening Edit — a real regression in the edit-receipt flow possibly introduced while wiring ledger history button or correction logic, which blocks the documented primary flow (R54/R55) from completing at all. This must be fixed since the task explicitly requires 'the primary flow edits a receipt, opens its History and sees the correction, and sees the Verified status in Settings' to work.

Given the primary flow is broken and 11 acceptance tests fail, requirements R18, R19 (verifyLedger reliability), R13/R14 (append-only correctness for created receipts), R26/R27 (verification line format), R28 (export entry code field format), R34 (unknown code handling), R35/R39 (backup ledger completeness), R54/R55 (ui_flow primary path) are not reliably satisfied even though files exist.
feedback: Good overall structure and file layout, but the core verifyLedger tamper-detection logic has real bugs (reordering detected as 'missing', missing-entry detection broken), addReceipt doesn't append a receipt.created ledger entry (so normal receipt creation doesn't grow the ledger, breaking R14's append-only guarantee), the CSV verification line format doesn't match the documented/expected '# verification: entries=N, headHash=H, code=C' textual format, the verification code's length/representation is inconsistent between ledger.ts (76-char combined code) and tests/usages expecting a bare 12-char code, verifyExportCode rejects valid-looking 64-char unknown codes with a format error instead of reporting them as not-from-this-app, and backup restore loses ledger entries. Additionally the UI primary flow (edit receipt → History → Settings verified) is currently broken per static validation because the Save button stays disabled, which is a blocking regression. Please fix the verifyLedger logic to correctly distinguish missing vs reordered vs prevHash-mismatch cases with correct firstBadSeq, make receipt creation append a ledger entry directly, standardize on one verification-code representation across ledger.ts/exportCsv.ts/exportPdf.ts/exportVerification.ts, fix the CSV verification line format, loosen the code format check in verifyExportCode for unknown codes, ensure backup/restore preserves/imports the full ledger, and fix the edit-receipt form so Save becomes enabled again after editing.
